FDA Approved: No Brand name: Mim8 Generic name: denecimig Company: Novo Nordisk Treatment for: Hemophilia A, Hemophilia A with Inhibitors Add Drugs.com on Google Mim8 (denecimig) is an investigational FVIIIa mimetic bispecific antibody in development for the prophylaxis of hemophilia A regardless of inhibitor status. * Hemophilia is a rare inherited bleeding disorder that impairs the body's ability to make blood clots, a process needed to stop bleeding. Hemophilia A is caused by a missing or defective clotting Factor VIII (FVIII). Some people with hemophilia A may develop inhibitors, an immune system response to the clotting factors used in replacement therapy, which can cause treatment to become ineffective. * Mim8 (denecimig) "mimics" the role of activated FVIII (FVIIIa) by bridging Factor IXa and Factor X. This action replaces FVIIIa function, which helps restore the body's thrombin generation capacity, helping blood to clot. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Microsoft Word - 03112026 DUR Memo (https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/okhca/docs/about/boards-and-committees/dur/2026/march/03112026%20DUR%20Packet.pdf) citeturn336search12 [wordlim: 200] Published: 8 months ago; Anticipated FDA Response ... denecimig (Mim8) ... 09/29/2026 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Mim8 is not yet approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Determination of safety and efficacy by the FDA has not yet been made, and the date of product approval is not known at this time. Under-the-skin injection to prevent bleeding episodes in adults and children with hemophilia A, including people with inhibitors (antibodies that stop standard factor VIII replacement from working). It mimics the job of factor VIII, the clotting protein people with hemophilia A lack, and can be given once a month, every 2 weeks or weekly from a single-use prefilled pen.
